lxc_cab07f2b7f8f842a.text: Borough Market's story goes back about 1,000 years, when people sold food near London Bridge.

lxc_9cbca7e8560d9398.text: In 1756, local parishioners moved it to the place where it stands today.

lxc_4bb517d5bb2ff4c0.text: The market is now a charity.

lxc_bb198aed13f644d7.text: Volunteer trustees run it for shoppers, traders and neighbours, so it is still a community place, not only a tourist sight.

lxc_207c820932f50b0f.text: More than 100 businesses sell food there.

lxc_9b59bde0bfc05781.text: Applebee's offers British seafood, Arabica serves Middle Eastern meze, falafel and shawarma, and Bao Borough makes bao buns.

lxc_d988a7078b3f10cc.text: Visitors can shop for cheese and other ingredients, choose a hot lunch, and meet some of the people who feed London today.

lxc_ded495c85983412b.text: Marché des Enfants Rouges is Paris's oldest covered food market.

lxc_fc4a6872886ac40a.text: Its unusual name means “Market of the Red Children.”

lxc_4b6866a3b8384667.text: It remembers children from a nearby home who wore red clothes.

lxc_1c35e46e693f723f.text: In the 1990s, there was a plan to replace the old market with a car park.

lxc_a070f737e6076d8e.text: Traders and neighbours protested and even slept outside to save it.

lxc_007337b0d05b6572.text: Today, their market is full of different people and foods.

lxc_ed13ebb8128b65b3.text: Tom's team serves Moroccan chicken skewers and couscous.

lxc_77e16f22e204ffd4.text: Julienne cooks Creole food with flavours from Cameroon.

lxc_1331f5a2ec846a36.text: Visitors can also buy farm cheese, Breton buckwheat galettes, oysters, fresh fruit juice, and organic fruit and vegetables.

lxc_fd82e1c2c49e9a4d.text: Visit three famous food markets in Barcelona, Paris and London.

lxc_e80e8b93a16b14ce.text: Meet the farmers, neighbours, cooks and traders who shaped them, discover what people eat there today, then use practical English to buy food, check ingredients, pay and tip.

lxc_d4e3e259543600e8.text: La Boqueria stands on La Rambla, but its story began before the covered market.

lxc_0d4a81deb2a58472.text: In 1217, records described meat stalls there.

lxc_3873c25efdb3d56e.text: Many early sellers were farmers from villages around Barcelona, bringing food into the city.

lxc_81c1040609b506ef.text: Traders moved to the present site in 1836.

lxc_0a2a0fe8b03364d0.text: Today, more than 200 traders open their shutters.

lxc_928cfd1ed2c7b1c7.text: Visitors pass bright fruit and vegetables, olives and preserved foods, meat, fish and seafood.

lxc_81b5bc4d6e995254.text: Small bars serve food beside the shopping stalls.

lxc_8fe415426f782d33.text: The market still connects two groups: people who sell food and people who come to shop, eat and talk.

lxc_9159d3d86279a1a0.text: It has a long history, but it is also part of everyday city life.

lxc_05a603fe195ffdd4.text: Tipping customs change between Spain, France and the UK.

lxc_9bc67a656b37a6ea.text: At a simple market stall or self-service counter, people normally pay the displayed price unless the seller says otherwise.

lxc_810c6ef15fea1a5e.text: In Spain, a tip is optional, and some people simply round up the bill.

lxc_39b01d3997bf38b8.text: In France, restaurant prices normally include service, so extra money is optional.

lxc_95ccfbdb9154f2ae.text: In the UK, a restaurant bill may include a discretionary or compulsory service charge.

lxc_4aede9a35b347d31.text: A visitor should read the bill before adding more money.

lxc_da901e232a34f6a9.text: The rules can feel different, but you do not need to guess.

lxc_3a23d347940c0bf3.text: The safest habit in all three countries is simple: check the bill, then ask.
